decisions.rationale: dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 166158, so no exact-duplicate row handling is required.

These non-drop columns are all required with null_rate 0.0 (year, month, day, carrier, flight, origin, sched_dep_time) and together plausibly identify one scheduled flight departure, since tailnum (0.9% null) and actual dep_time (2.9% null) cannot serve as reliable keys.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry no business meaning, so all three are dropped.

dep_time, sched_dep_time, arr_time, and sched_arr_time all show max values of 2359.0-2400.0, an hhmm clock encoding that is not a valid TIME or TIMESTAMP value, so these are cast to INTEGER rather than a temporal type.

dep_time/dep_delay (null_rate 0.029388), arr_time (0.0307), and arr_delay/air_time (0.032981) share similar null rates, consistent with cancelled or diverted flights lacking actual timing data; nulls are retained, not imputed.
tailnum has null_rate 0.009154 (1521 of 166158 rows), a small but nonzero rate, so the column is kept nullable rather than required.

purpose: silver_nyc_flights provides cleaned, typed flight-level records for the 2013 NYC-area flights dataset (departures from EWR, JFK, and LGA), feeding downstream analytics on flight delays, schedules, carriers, and travel patterns.
usage: Consumers should join or filter on the declared grain (year, month, day, carrier, flight, origin, sched_dep_time) to obtain one record per scheduled departure, and must handle nulls deliberately in dep_time, dep_delay, arr_time, arr_delay, and air_time (roughly 2.9% to 3.3% null), which represent flights without recorded actual timing (e.g. cancellations); hhmm-encoded time columns (dep_time, sched_dep_time, arr_time, sched_arr_time) remain integers, not clock/timestamp types, and require hour/minute decoding by the consumer if needed.
limitations: This cleanup does not resolve the roughly 2.9%-3.3% null rates in actual departure/arrival times and delays, nor the 0.9% null rate in tailnum; these are retained as nulls rather than imputed or dropped. The hhmm-encoded time fields are not cast to TIME/TIMESTAMP because values up to 2400 are not valid clock times, so any time-of-day derivation is left to downstream consumers. No duplicate rows were found (duplicate_row_rate 0.0), so no deduplication logic was applied.
